sections.title: Market Pulse: Tech Rally Continues, Futures Higher on Tuesday

items.headline: U.S. Futures Point to Higher Open Following Monday's Tech-Led Gains
items.summary: U.S. stock futures are trending higher on Tuesday, October 6, indicating a positive open, as Wall Street looks to build on Monday's rally driven by technology stocks. This comes despite persistent elevated Treasury yields and ongoing geopolitical concerns. Crude oil prices are retreating, allowing investors to focus on strong earnings growth estimates.

items.headline: Technology Sector Leads S&P 500 Gains on Monday
items.summary: The technology sector was a primary driver of the S&P 500's positive performance on Monday, with the Nasdaq Composite hitting a new record high. This rally is fueled by continued enthusiasm for artificial intelligence and strong earnings growth expectations.

items.headline: Communication Services, Materials, and Energy Lead Sector Performance
items.summary: On Monday, ten out of eleven S&P 500 broad sectors closed in positive territory. The Communication Services ($XLC), Materials ($XLB), and Energy ($XLE) Select Sector SPDRs were among the top performers, rising 1.1%, 1.2%, and 0.9% respectively. The Real Estate sector ($XLRE) was the only laggard, declining by 0.4%.

items.headline: Economic Data Shows Services Sector Expansion; Key Reports Due Today
items.summary: The Institute of Supply Management reported that the services purchasing managers index reached 54.9%, indicating an expansion in services activities and aligning with consensus estimates. Today, the ADP Weekly Employment Change and the International Trade in Goods and Services report are scheduled for release.

items.headline: Earnings Season Kicks Off with Key Company Reports
items.summary: The third-quarter earnings season is underway, with several major companies scheduled to report today, October 6, 2026. Companies in focus include Constellation Brands Inc. ($STZ), RPM International Inc. ($RPM), Lamb Weston Holdings Inc. ($LW), and Neogen Corporation ($NEOG). Earnings growth estimates for the upcoming season have been revised upward to nearly 30%.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Remain Elevated, Fed Rate Hike Odds Reduced
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield continues to trade above 5.3%, a level last seen in 2002, while the 30-year yield breached 5.7%. However, a soft September jobs report has significantly reduced expectations of an October Fed rate hike, with markets currently assigning a less than 20% probability of a rate increase this month.

items.headline: Oil Prices Retreat as G7 Releases Reserves
items.summary: Crude oil prices have retreated after the Group of Seven (G7) nations announced the release of 100 million barrels of reserves over the next four months. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell 1.86% to $87.77 per barrel, and Brent crude dropped 1.64% to $98.67 per barrel.
